I will not start from empty. I will do close to what worked for me last year and what the good growers around me do. With 36 mu, I cannot fuss over every row by hand, so I will keep most land in maize because maize is steady here and I have well water. I will still keep some cotton because if I manage water and spray on time, it still brings cash, and I will leave a smaller piece for mungbean because it is cheaper to plant and does not need as much fertilizer. I did not study books, so I count money and look at the field. If I cut fertilizer too hard and yield falls, that hurts more than wasting a little. So I will feed maize a bit heavier, cotton steady, and mungbean light. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, plough or rotary once, put base fertilizer down first, then chase with nitrogen later, and water about 3 times if rain is not enough. For cotton, I will use an improved seed, plough the field clean, put enough base fertilizer, and spray more times because insects on cotton can ruin the crop fast. For mungbean, I will keep it simple: less nitrogen, some phosphate, one light watering if dry, and a couple of sprays if insects show. I also have family labor limited because some people work outside, so I will choose a plan I can actually finish on time.
